citations.assessment: The selected Menachot places Rabbi Hiyya and Rav Aha son of Rav Avya together in the tefillin discussion and has a separate Rav Ashi–Amemar scene. The narrator’s reported Avya/Avya wording represents another witness, not a reading adopted in translation.
Chullin explicitly gives Rabbah bar Rav Huna as the question’s addressee. Its following avian diversion and Rashi’s explanation are directly present.

The Arukh’s direct entry explicitly cites both Beitzah and Chullin, explaining the support as appointment and seating at the head of the academy. This confirms the lexicographer’s interpretation without fixing external chronology.

Beitzah gives Rav Huna rather than his son as Avya’s interlocutor, and Rashi explicitly identifies Rabbah as Rav Huna’s son addressing his father. The Chida agrees on the family roles but disputes Heilprin’s explanation of why Rashi glosses them.

holds.raw: רבא בריה דרב אויא סבא לרב אשי מנחות
holds.reason: The selected Menachot reading is Aha son of Rav Avya. Rav Ashi’s exchange with Amemar then begins as a separate scene. The Chida explicitly allows an alternate Menachot witness underlying Yuhasin and rejects attributing an elementary confusion to him. Keep the exact Yuhasin print passage unverified and reflect this later disagreement.

holds.raw: מ"ש היוחסין באות א' רב אויא סבא דגברא רבה הוא וכן רבה ברב הונא לרבא ברי'
holds.reason: The direct Yuhasin alphabetical transcription has no available Aleph section. The Chida directly quotes the sentence in discussion, but reads it as Rabbah speaking to Rabbah’s own son. The Chida’s quotation and explanation constitute a secondary witness to the exact wording.

holds.raw: רב אחא ברי' דרב אויא סבא שאמר לרב אשי יותר מעשר פעמים
holds.reason: The sampled passages explicitly make Rav Aha the challenger or interlocutor. They show that this is a recurring formula. The exact count and use of the epithet in every passage remain Heilprin’s report.
Sherira’s epistle expressly gives Rav Huna forty years. The author’s proposed succession date for the son and application of that calculation to this episode remain an inference.

holds.raw: אבל נכון יותר גירסת ש"ס החדשים רב אחא
holds.reason: The named Aha reading is present in the selected Menachot. Neither that witness nor the abbreviated title identifies the exact edition with the attributed early modern glosses. Keep the preference as the narrator’s.

notes.text: The paired Chullin and Beitzah exchanges have different generations and both are visible in the checked sources. The Arukh and Rashi explain the phrase differently. Petach Einayim agrees on the two narratives and disputes Heilprin’s reconstruction of Yuhasin. The exact Yuhasin print and new-Shas witnesses and the historical chronology remain qualified.
